note: Manifest ingestion contract for official state and territorial sources. A state entry is hash-verified and its metadata validated, then recorded in source_status as registered_not_indexed: no state parser exists, so no state text enters the provision index and no state-law coverage is claimed (topic state_law stays not_acquired). An entry from a host that is not listed as a confirmed official host for its jurisdiction is rejected. Hosts are added here only after the publisher's own site has been confirmed under an operator-authorised acquisition task; the list starts empty. A host is listed only with documented publisher identity and endpoint evidence (S7-P1-48 evidence file); each host is limited to the source classes it serves. No publisher page reviewed grants or denies bulk reuse, so no reuse permission is inferred: an entry may claim usage_status permitted only with rights.permission_reference naming an operator decision. From v0.3 every approved host and every host/source-class pair must cite a valid, host-matching record in state_source_evidence.json by evidence_id (see its validity_policy); an approval whose evidence is missing, malformed, stale, on another or an unapproved host, or at the wrong level is not honoured. From v0.4 (S7-P1-59) two further evidence rules apply: a source-class record is not honoured when another host-level record on the same host has the same sha256 and byte count, because a response indistinguishable from the entry page does not establish a source class; and a redirect chain relied on for a non-https requested_url must start at requested_url and be contiguous (each hop's "to" equals the next hop's "from"). Approvals weaken only when evidence is indistinguishable or malformed. From v0.5 (S7-P1-60) a host declaring endpoint_basis index_page_only (a value from endpoint_bases) stays an approved host but establishes none of its source classes, because entry-page evidence does not show an endpoint serving them.
